scenes.tts: How do you prove where a cell was born, when a stain shows only its shape?
scenes.visual: Title card: Marked in the Yolk Sac. A stained microglial cell with a question mark over its origin.
scenes.narration: How do you prove where a cell was born, when a stain shows only its shape?

scenes.tts: Mark a progenitor, then look for the mark later in everything it made. That is fate mapping.
scenes.visual: One progenitor turns green; its descendants, generations later, are all green.
scenes.narration: Mark a progenitor, then look for the mark later in everything it made. That is fate mapping.

scenes.tts: The modern version uses an enzyme called Cree. It cuts and rejoins DNA at two short sequences called lox P sites.
scenes.caption: The modern version uses an enzyme called Cre. It cuts and rejoins DNA at two short sequences called loxP sites.
scenes.visual: Cartoon of DNA: two loxP triangles in the same orientation flank a red STOP block in front of a reporter gene. Cre brings the two sites together.
scenes.narration: The modern version uses an enzyme called Cre. It cuts and rejoins DNA at two short sequences called loxP sites.

scenes.tts: In a reporter mouse, Cree removes a stop sequence between the sites. The reporter turns on, and every descendant inherits it.
scenes.caption: In a reporter mouse, Cre removes a stop sequence between the sites. The reporter turns on, and every descendant inherits it.
scenes.visual: The STOP block is cut out, leaving one loxP site; the reporter switches on; the cell divides and every daughter glows.
scenes.narration: In a reporter mouse, Cre removes a stop sequence between the sites. The reporter turns on, and every descendant inherits it.

scenes.tts: Make Cree from a gene the progenitor uses. In the line used for microglia, one dose of tamoxifen lets it act for about a day.
scenes.caption: Make Cre from a gene the progenitor uses. In the line used for microglia, one dose of tamoxifen lets it act for about a day.
scenes.visual: Promoter drives Cre. A timeline with a one-day window opened by a tamoxifen drop; only cells using the gene inside the window glow.
scenes.narration: Make Cre from a gene the progenitor uses. In the line used for microglia, one dose of tamoxifen lets it act for about a day.

scenes.tts: In twenty ten, Florent Ginhoux, Miriam Merad and colleagues did this in mice. The Cree was driven by Runx one.
scenes.caption: In 2010, Florent Ginhoux, Miriam Merad and colleagues did this in mice. The Cre was driven by Runx1.
scenes.visual: Label: Ginhoux, Merad and colleagues, 2010, mouse. Runx1-CreER.
scenes.narration: In 2010, Florent Ginhoux, Miriam Merad and colleagues did this in mice. The Cre was driven by Runx1.

scenes.tts: A pulse at embryonic day seven and a half marked early progenitors. Later, about a third of yolk-sac macrophages carried the mark.
scenes.caption: A pulse at embryonic day 7.5 marked early progenitors. Later, about a third of yolk-sac macrophages carried the mark.
scenes.visual: Tamoxifen at E7.5 marks some Runx1-positive yolk-sac progenitors. Arrow to a later embryo: yolk-sac macrophages, one in three glowing.
scenes.narration: A pulse at embryonic day 7.5 marked early progenitors. Later, about a third of yolk-sac macrophages carried the mark.

scenes.tts: Call the yolk-sac labeling thirty percent. Suppose very few blood-making cells are marked, say two percent.
scenes.caption: Call the yolk-sac labeling 30 percent. Suppose very few blood-making cells are marked, say 2 percent.
scenes.visual: Two source boxes: yolk sac 30%, blood 2%.
scenes.narration: Call the yolk-sac labeling 30 percent. Suppose very few blood-making cells are marked, say 2 percent.

scenes.tts: What share of adult microglia should be marked? Try all from the yolk sac, half, or all from blood.
scenes.visual: Three empty bars: all yolk sac, half and half, all blood. Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: What share of adult microglia should be marked? Try all from the yolk sac, half, or all from blood.

scenes.tts: Each cell carries the mark or not. If all sources expand alike, the marked share mirrors the mix.
scenes.visual: Assumption note beside the bars: sources expand alike, no third source. Bars fill in turn: 30%, then 16% with the working on screen (average of 30% and 2%), then 2%.
scenes.narration: Each cell carries the mark or not. If all sources expand alike, the marked share mirrors the mix.

scenes.tts: All from the yolk sac predicts about thirty percent. Half and half, about sixteen. All blood, about two.
scenes.caption: All from the yolk sac predicts about 30 percent. Half and half, about 16. All blood, about 2.
scenes.visual: The three bars stay filled: 30%, 16%, 2%.
scenes.narration: All from the yolk sac predicts about 30 percent. Half and half, about 16. All blood, about 2.

scenes.tts: In adults, about a third of microglia carried the mark. Very few blood cells did.
scenes.visual: Observed bar drops in at about a third, beside a near-empty blood bar.
scenes.narration: In adults, about a third of microglia carried the mark. Very few blood cells did.

scenes.tts: That is the top bar. Later pulses marked blood, but few microglia.
scenes.visual: Observed bar sits beside bar 1. Inset: later pulse, blood bright, microglia dim.
scenes.narration: That is the top bar. Later pulses marked blood, but few microglia.

scenes.tts: Read alone, a third sounds like a minority. Read against a source labeled at a third, it means most.
scenes.visual: Two readings side by side: 'a third = minority' crossed out; 'a third, from a source labeled at a third = most'.
scenes.narration: Read alone, a third sounds like a minority. Read against a source labeled at a third, it means most.

scenes.tts: The reading depends on the source. If the adult count is thirty percent and the true source were forty percent labeled, about three quarters came from the yolk sac.
scenes.caption: The reading depends on the source. If the adult count is 30 percent and the true source were 40 percent labeled, about three quarters came from the yolk sac.
scenes.visual: Sensitivity card, adult count 30%: source labeled 30% gives all; source labeled 40% gives about three-quarters, (30 − 2) ÷ (40 − 2). Label: illustration, not a measurement.
scenes.narration: The reading depends on the source. If the adult count is 30 percent and the true source were 40 percent labeled, about three quarters came from the yolk sac.

scenes.tts: So the right word is most, and possibly all. The data cannot give an exact number.
scenes.visual: Card: most, possibly all, not an exact number.
scenes.narration: So the right word is most, and possibly all. The data cannot give an exact number.

scenes.tts: Embryos lacking N C X one, which the heart needs to beat, still made yolk-sac macrophages.
scenes.caption: Embryos lacking Ncx1, which the heart needs to beat, still made yolk-sac macrophages.
scenes.visual: An Ncx1 embryo with no heartbeat; yolk sac full of gold macrophages.
scenes.narration: Embryos lacking Ncx1, which the heart needs to beat, still made yolk-sac macrophages.

scenes.tts: But they had no brain microglia. So the progenitors travel in through the early circulation.
scenes.visual: The brain of the Ncx1 embryo is empty. A normal embryo beside it shows gold cells flowing through vessels to the head.
scenes.narration: But they had no brain microglia. So the progenitors travel in through the early circulation.

scenes.tts: Microglia also need the receptor C S F one R. Mice without it have few or none.
scenes.caption: Microglia also need the receptor CSF1R. Mice without it have few or none.
scenes.visual: Label: CSF1R. Brain without CSF1R: almost no microglia.
scenes.narration: Microglia also need the receptor CSF1R. Mice without it have few or none.

scenes.tts: In healthy adult mice, microglia renew themselves. Blood monocytes do not replace them.
scenes.visual: Adult brain: a microglial cell divides; monocytes stay in vessels.
scenes.narration: In healthy adult mice, microglia renew themselves. Blood monocytes do not replace them.

scenes.tts: So read a fate map against its source. In mice, most microglia were born in the yolk sac.
scenes.visual: Closing card: read the label against the source. In mice, most microglia come from the yolk sac.
scenes.narration: So read a fate map against its source. In mice, most microglia were born in the yolk sac.
